provenance: All examples are fictional teaching examples written for this repository. They are not user records, case histories, diagnoses, or evidence.
rules: example mode never reads user-entered answers
example mode never writes into exercise answer fields
examples must remain low-risk and non-diagnostic
synthetic examples are teaching projections, not medical evidence

thought-record-7: A meeting started before I had my notes ready.
I stumbled over my first sentence.
The meeting continued normally and two people asked useful follow-up questions.
I was flustered at the start, but that does not show what everyone thinks of my competence.
Still uncomfortable, but less certain of the original thought.
catch-check-change: I am going to fail this entire project.
Fact: one test is failing. Prediction: the whole project will fail.
One test is failing; I can inspect that failure before judging the project.
loop-map: I will make it worse if I reply.
Avoided opening the thread for two days.
The unanswered email felt larger and the original prediction felt more convincing.
tiny-step: It feels too large to start.
Open the document and write three headings.
Whether the structure becomes clearer after the headings exist.
problem-solving: I keep missing a weekly study block.
Move it earlier; shorten it; pair it with an existing routine.
Earlier is quieter but conflicts with breakfast; shorter is easier but covers less; pairing gives a reminder.
affect-to-action: One unit test is failing; 'I broke everything' is a judgement.
A failing test identifies a specific mismatch I can inspect.
Run only the failing test and inspect the first assertion.
Use the result to choose the next debugging step.
worry-time: What if I forget something important tomorrow?
Yes, I can make a short checklist.
Write the checklist now, then park the remaining what-ifs for 6:30 pm worry time.
At 6:30 pm, only one worry still seems actionable.
Close the note and return attention to the evening routine.
graded-task-ladder: 1) cup away; 2) stack papers; 3) bin rubbish; 4) clear one working space; 5) sort the remaining papers.
The whole desk did not need to be solved before it became usable.
behavioural-experiment: If I ask one clarifying question, everyone will think I was not listening.
Ask one ordinary clarification in a low-stakes team discussion.
The question was answered and the discussion continued.
The prediction did not occur in this instance; one observation does not prove how every group will react.
setback-plan: I start cancelling ordinary plans and staying up much later.
Thoughts become more all-or-nothing; I feel flat; routines slip; sleep changes.
Return to a simple sleep/wake routine, reduce optional load, use the thought record, contact a trusted person.
Trusted friend and usual health professional if symptoms persist or worsen.
Escalating distress, safety concerns, or being unable to manage ordinary needs means routine self-help is no longer enough.
